requirements.requirement: Add at least 512 MB of active, disk-backed swap on node1.
requirements.summary: A fully allocated, root-owned 536,870,912-byte file was initialized as swap. The active swap table shows 524,284 KiB of usable file-backed swap after activation and again after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Ensure the added swap activates at boot.
requirements.summary: The swapfile was added to /etc/fstab, was healthy before restart, and automatically returned active after a confirmed reboot with a different boot identity.

requirements.requirement: Prefer the new swap over existing swap.
requirements.summary: Before and after reboot, the new swapfile had priority 100 while the existing /dev/vda2 swap had priority -2.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: RHEL 7.9 and kernel 3.10.0-1160.el7.x86_64 remained unchanged across the work and reboot. The implementation used native tools already present on the platform.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. Direct pre- and post-reboot evidence proves the new disk-backed swap is active, boot-persistent, and preferred, while the OS release and kernel remain unchanged. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete and independently corroborated by lifecycle boot identities; only minor retained backup/log residue affects hygiene.
limitations: Native package-manager consistency checks timed out both before and after execution, so package health could not be independently compared.

The lifecycle snapshots do not directly inventory swap or /etc/fstab; final swap and persistence conclusions therefore rely on the captured executor commands, which are coherent and include a demonstrated reboot transition.

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive mutations—creating and securing the swapfile, initializing and enabling it, updating fstab, activating swap, and rebooting—had clear task or mandatory restart-protocol roles. No failed services or new network exposure remained. Two minor task-generated artifacts were not cleaned up: /etc/fstab.pre-antrieb-swap, a justified rollback backup retained after successful validation, and /tmp/antrieb-reboot.log, a restart-scheduling log retained after use. Neither was reverted. No unrelated troubleshooting mutations were observed.
